negative_findings.description: No MK security-printing or cash-in-transit (CIT) supplier was identified despite a dedicated Macedonian-language search ('заштитно печатење чекови картички', 'обезбедување транспорт на пари').
negative_findings.result_summary: Results returned only banking law, NBRM check regulation and generic payment-security pages — no named banknote/cheque printer or CIT/cash-handling company serving MK banks.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cash-handling and security-printing suppliers are an explicit part of this cell; without them the supplier map is incomplete on the physical-cash side.

negative_findings.description: Searching for POS/ATM distributors and maintenance firms in Macedonian returned only bank product pages, not supplier pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query 'дистрибутер POS терминали Македонија банкомати одржување компанија Скопје' surfaced kb.com.mk, stb.com.mk, ohridskabanka.mk tariff pages instead of vendors; bank-side pages dominate the term space.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: 'ПОС терминал' and 'банкомат' are noisy terms owned by bank marketing pages; supplier discovery needs company-name-first queries or procurement/job-ad proxies instead.

negative_findings.description: No Macedonia-specific country page for Printec or a local Payten/ASEE MK entity site was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Printec search resolved to the Bulgaria country page plus an expired MK job ad; Payten MK query returned mostly Bulgarian results and unrelated PayNet terminals.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Two of the most likely bank-equipment suppliers in MK lack a confirmed local URL, so their MK activity must currently be inferred from job ads and group-level releases.

negative_findings.description: Duna Computers' own corporate domain was not confirmed; only Facebook, ZoomInfo and a SeeNews interview were found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned social and third-party profiles rather than a first-party site.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: First-party reference pages are the highest-value artefact for 'we delivered' claims; this one is missing from the collection plan.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash-handling, CIT and security-printing / card-body suppliers to MK banks are entirely unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search MK company registry and directories by activity code for 'обезбедување', 'превоз на пари', 'печатница' and cross-check bank annual reports and NBRM cash-cycle documents for named service providers.

coverage_gaps.description: LinkedIn 'we won / we delivered' posts — the cell's stated highest-value channel — were only sampled indirectly via search engines, not systematically covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Set up analyst-led or licensed monitoring of LinkedIn company pages for CaSys, KIBS, Nextsense, Semos, Duna, Netcetera, Printec MK, ASEE/Payten; avoid ToS-violating scraping.

coverage_gaps.description: The supplier roster is anchored on ~8 well-known firms; the long tail of smaller MK integrators (MASIT's 100+ members, IT.mk IT Index) has not been enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a one-off full crawl of masit.org.mk member pages and the IT.mk IT Index, then filter for banking/payments capability keywords to extend the actor map.

coverage_gaps.description: Global-vendor channel-partner directories were only sampled once (Thales/Nextsense).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically query partner locators for NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Verifone, Ingenico, Entrust, Idemia, Temenos, Oracle FS and Microsoft filtered to North Macedonia to reveal which local firms hold which authorisations.

coverage_gaps.description: Albanian-language coverage was not attempted, though a significant share of MK business communication and some suppliers operate in Albanian.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add Albanian query terms (kompani IT Shkup, terminale POS, personalizim kartash, banka) in a follow-up pass, even though the run scope lists only mk/en.

brief: The MK local supplier landscape for banking/payments is small and highly concentrated: CaSys (the only domestic card processor and certified personalisation bureau) and bank-owned KIBS (clearing, digital trust) are the two structural nodes, surrounded by a handful of integrators — Nextsense, Semos, Duna, Netcetera, plus regional players Printec and Asseco SEE/Payten with local operations. Award-level detail is rarely published by banks, so it surfaces instead in supplier news pages, vendor-supplied PR on faktor.mk / bankarstvo.mk / ecommerce.mk, e-Nabavki contract PDFs that name the same suppliers on public-sector deals, and LinkedIn posts. Pointer sources — MASIT's member directory, the IT.mk IT Index, zk.mk and CompanyWall — are the practical route to enumerating the long tail of smaller integrators and resolving Cyrillic/Latin name variants. The clearest blind spots are cash-handling/CIT and security-printing suppliers, for which no named MK company was found in Macedonian-language search, and systematic LinkedIn monitoring, which needs an access-compliant method rather than search-engine sampling.
